aids.description_en: Financial assistance for low-income Singaporeans experiencing temporary difficulties. Up to S$1,000/month per household. Provides cash, medical, and social service support. Administered by Social Service Offices (SSOs). Duration up to 24 months, renewable with review.
aids.organisme: Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) / Social Service Offices

aids.description_en: Quarterly top-up to CPF Retirement Account for elderly Singaporeans with limited savings and low lifetime income. 2025 quarterly amounts: S$600 (HDB 4-room), S$750 (HDB 3-room), S$900 (HDB 1-2 room). Benefits approximately 150,000 seniors per year.
aids.organisme: Ministry of Finance / Central Provident Fund (CPF)

aids.description_en: Annual cash payment to low-to-middle income Singaporeans to help offset GST impact. 2025 amounts: S$850 for income ≤S$34,000 (Assessable Income), S$450 for income S$34,001–S$100,000. Deposited directly to bank account or PayNow-NRIC.

Supplement for low-wage workers aged 35+. 2025 maximum: S$4,200/year for workers aged 60+ in regular employment. Paid 10% cash + 90% CPF contributions. Self-employed persons receive 10% cash + 90% Medisave. Encourages employment and CPF savings.

Cash gift and co-saving for newborns. 1st child: S$3,000 cash gift + S$3,000 Child Development Account (CDA) co-savings = S$6,000 total. 2nd child: S$3,000 cash gift + S$5,000 CDA. 3rd child onwards: S$4,000 cash gift + S$9,000 CDA = S$13,000. Enhanced Baby Support Grant (S$3,000 extra) from 14 Feb 2024.
aids.organisme: Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF)

aids.description_en: Mandatory universal health insurance for all Singapore citizens and PRs. Covers large hospitalization bills and selected costly outpatient treatments. Low-income Singaporeans receive premium subsidies via MediShield Life Premium Subsidies (up to 100% for lowest-income). Administered by CPF Board.

Means-tested subsidy for after-school student care programmes. Maximum subsidy: S$290/month for households with monthly per capita income ≤S$1,100. Graduated subsidy scale to S$1,580/month per capita income. Available at MOE Student Care Centres in primary schools.

Integrated early childhood development programme for children aged 0–6 from lower-income families. Provides developmental screenings, parenting support, early intervention, and centre-based care subsidies. Referral-based. Target households: per capita income ≤S$900/month.
aids.organisme: Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) / Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA)

aids.description_en: Subsidised GP and dental visits at participating clinics for Singapore citizens. Blue card (lower income): up to S$80 subsidy per GP visit, S$265 per dental visit. Orange card (middle income): up to S$20/GP, S$100/dental. Pioneer Generation: higher subsidies including free dental scaling.
aids.organisme: Ministry of Health (MOH) / Agency for Integrated Care (AIC)

aids.nom: HOPE — Home Ownership Plus Education Scheme
aids.description_en: Combined housing and education scheme for low-income families with 2 or fewer children who are willing to undergo family planning. Provides subsidised HDB flat purchase and educational bursaries of S$700/year per child in higher institutions. Managed by Eurasian Association and MCCY.
aids.organisme: Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) / Eurasian Association
